title: UML Class Diagrams Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on reading and drawing UML class diagrams: class boxes, visibility, relationship arrows, multiplicity, dependency and how to read common pattern diagrams.

chapters.title: Class Boxes, Attributes and Visibility
points: A class is a 3-compartment box: name on top, attributes in the middle, operations at the bottom; the name is bold and centred, abstract class names are in italics
Attribute syntax: visibility name : type = default, e.g. - balance : double = 0.0
Operation syntax: visibility name(param : type) : returnType, e.g. + deposit(amount : double) : void
Visibility markers: + public, - private, # protected, ~ package; attributes are normally private and operations public
Static members are underlined, abstract operations are in italics, and an interface is marked with the <<interface>> stereotype above its name

chapters.title: Association, Aggregation and Composition
points: Association is a plain solid line meaning 'uses or knows about'; an open arrowhead makes it navigable in one direction only (A knows B, B does not know A)
Aggregation is a solid line with a hollow diamond at the whole's end: a 'has-a' relation where the part can live without the whole (Team has Players)
Composition is a solid line with a filled diamond at the whole's end: a strong 'owns-a' relation where deleting the whole deletes the parts (House owns Rooms)
The diamond always sits on the container (whole) side, never on the part side
Lifecycle test to pick one: part outlives the whole means aggregation; part dies with the whole means composition; just a reference means association

chapters.title: Inheritance, Realization and Dependency
points: Inheritance (generalization) is a solid line with a hollow triangle pointing to the parent: 'is-a', e.g. Dog -> Animal
Realization is a dashed line with a hollow triangle pointing to the interface: a class implements an interface, e.g. ArrayList ..|> List
Dependency is a dashed line with an open arrow from the user to the used class: a weak, temporary 'uses' link, such as a parameter type or local variable
Strength order from weakest to strongest: dependency, association, aggregation, composition, inheritance
Common mix-up: solid line + hollow triangle = inheritance, dashed line + hollow triangle = realization, dashed line + open arrow = dependency

chapters.title: Multiplicity and Reading Relationships
points: Multiplicity is written at each end of a line: 1 (exactly one), 0..1 (optional), * or 0..* (zero or more), 1..* (at least one), n..m (a range)
Read multiplicity at an end as 'how many of that end's class relate to one instance of the other class': Customer 1 --- 0..* Order means one customer has many orders
Role names and labels sit on the line (e.g. +owner, +orders) and the attribute that implements a role is shown there instead of inside the box
An association class hangs off a line by a dashed connector to hold attributes of the link itself, e.g. Enrollment between Student and Course with grade
Many-to-many (* to *) is normally resolved with an association class or a join class, which turns it into two one-to-many links

chapters.title: Reading Pattern Diagrams and Common Mistakes
points: Reading routine: find the interface or abstract class first, follow triangles down to the concrete classes, then trace the diamonds and plain arrows for who holds what
Strategy pattern: Context holds a reference (association) to a Strategy interface, and ConcreteStrategies realize it, so the algorithm is swappable at runtime
Observer pattern: Subject aggregates 0..* Observer interface references, and ConcreteObservers realize Observer; Subject calls update() on each
Factory pattern: the Factory has a dependency (dashed arrow) on the concrete Products it creates and returns the Product interface type
Mistakes: diamond on the wrong end, solid triangle for realization, using inheritance for has-a, drawing every dependency and cluttering the diagram, omitting multiplicity

chapters.title: UML Class Diagram Cheat Sheet
points: Class box: Name / attributes / operations; visibility + public, - private, # protected, ~ package
Line notation: association = solid line; aggregation = solid + hollow diamond at whole; composition = solid + filled diamond at whole
Inheritance = solid line + hollow triangle to parent; realization = dashed line + hollow triangle to interface; dependency = dashed line + open arrow
Multiplicity: 1, 0..1, *, 1..*, n..m; read each end as 'how many of this class per one of the other'
Pattern reading order: interface first, then triangles to implementations, then diamonds and arrows for ownership and references
